findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the precedence/merge rule for combining the four prior_decision queries into one of the four values (e.g. 'any query showing recorded reasoning => explicit_justified; else any deliberate choice => explicit_bare; else incidental; else none').
evidence: 'It runs four deterministic queries ... and classifies what they return into exactly four values, with the record's content deciding'
No stated precedence when the four queries return conflicting evidence about deliberateness/reasoning
E2 signal (2): implicit acceptance criteria for the classification output when inputs disagree
findings.finding: The prior_decision classifier runs four independent deterministic queries (git log -S, git blame -L, ADR/docs grep, ticket-id grep) but the plan does not state how to resolve disagreement among them — e.g. when git log's commit trailer reads explicit_justified while the ADR grep returns none, or one query yields explicit_bare and another incidental. The plan says 'the record's content deciding' but with four record sources the precedence/merge rule is unstated.
findings.location: Edit 1 — 'prior_decision, an intent check' (the four-query block and four-value classification)
scenarios: A symbol whose commit trailer is bare but whose ADR records the reasoning: is it explicit_bare or explicit_justified?
git blame points to a refactor commit (incidental) while a ticket-id grep surfaces a deliberate decision ticket.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line resolution rule: take the strongest evidence across the four queries — reasoning present anywhere => explicit_justified; deliberate choice with no reasoning => explicit_bare; state without decision => incidental; nothing => none.

Edit 1: '...if it survives the floors, must still supply `evidence_changed` before its move reaches approval' — names an obligation but no enforcing step.
Edit 3 only says 'Surface the `prior_decision` record ... for a reversal what evidence has changed' — surfacing is not verifying that the field was supplied.

The Phase-2 penalty only scores the ABSENCE of naming at Phase 2 against the suggested remediation direction; a proposer's actual Phase-3 move could still omit `evidence_changed` with nothing catching it.
findings.finding: The `evidence_changed` requirement is stated as an unenforced obligation: no phase file gate blocks or flags a reversing move (one whose referenced finding is `explicit_justified`/`explicit_bare`) that omits `evidence_changed`, so an omission reaches Phase 4 unflagged — the exact failure mode the plan exists to close.
findings.location: Edit 2 (remediation.md) and Edit 3 (approval.md)
scenarios: A survivor whose Phase-2 remediation direction named changed evidence (so took no penalty and survived), but whose Phase-3 proposer produces a reversing move that omits `evidence_changed` — reaches Phase 4 with no flag.
A HARDENING/DEFECT finding with a `prior_decision` record where the proposer forgets the field; the reversal is presented to the user as an ordinary move.
findings.suggested_fix: In Edit 3 (approval.md), add that any item whose finding_refs include a non-`none` `prior_decision` finding is flagged to the reviewer as a reversal that either names its changed evidence (`evidence_changed` present) or is missing it — making omission visible at review; optionally, in Edit 2, state that the Plan-item constructor marks a reversing move lacking `evidence_changed` as `no-consensus` (carrying the prior_decision record) so it cannot be presented as a settled move.

SKILL.md/verification.md already acknowledge git may be absent: report section 'Trends (only if git history available)' (verification.md line 189).
Edit 2: Proposer A answers via 'web search plus the code' and the divergence research round is 'put symmetrically to both records'; no behaviour is stated if web search fails/returns nothing.
findings.finding: No fallback is specified for when prior_decision's git-dependent queries or the research round's web search cannot run (repo without git history, or web search unavailable) — the plan makes classification depend on 'what they return' but never states the value/behaviour when a query can't execute.
findings.location: Edit 1 (prior_decision query block) and Edit 2 (Proposer A / divergence research round)
scenarios: The audited repo has no git history: git log -S and git blame -L cannot run — is prior_decision then 'none', or is the whole check skipped?
Web search is disabled or errors: Proposer A (now the OSS-research proposer) and the divergence research round have no defined degraded outcome, so research-resolved vs no-consensus is undefined.

findings.location: Edit 1 (verification.md reclassification note) and Edit 2 (remediation.md), vs. Edit 3 (approval.md HARDENING flag)
findings.suggested_fix: Add `finding_type` to the Phase-2 survivor payload and to the remediation.md per-item schema in Edit 2's scope, defaulting to DEFECT and set to HARDENING on harm_reachable==no, so the label the reclassification note creates has an explicit path to the approval flag.

findings.finding: The new DEFECT/HARDENING classification enum is referenced as a label that must reach Phase-4 approval ('flag any item reclassified as HARDENING'), but Edit 2's Remediation Plan item schema is not given a field to carry it, and no phase is named as the point that assigns the default DEFECT label.
findings.location: Edit 1 (verification.md HARDENING reclassification) and Edit 2 (remediation.md Remediation Plan item) and Edit 3 (approval.md)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State harm_reachable's value vocabulary explicitly (yes | no | insufficient | na) and confirm 'insufficient'/'na' do not trigger the HARDENING reclassification (only '== no' does).
evidence: verification.md line 33: existing four sub-questions declared 'each `yes | no | insufficient | na`'.

Plan describes harm_reachable only via 'a no costs 1/5', 'over the answerable (non-na) set', and 'harm_reachable == "no" reclassifies' — implying yes/no/na but never enumerating insufficient, whose ordinal (0.5) affects the graded fraction.
findings.finding: harm_reachable is added as a fifth binary validity sub-question that participates in the graded fraction, but its own value vocabulary is never stated, unlike the existing four which are documented as 'yes | no | insufficient | na'.
findings.location: Edit 1 (verification.md) — harm_reachable sub-question and scoring bullet
scenarios: Verifier answers harm_reachable='insufficient' — is that a legal value contributing 0.5 to the denominator-of-5, and does it block or allow HARDENING reclassification (only '==no' reclassifies)?
findings.suggested_fix: Document harm_reachable with the same '`yes | no | insufficient | na`' vocabulary as the other four sub-questions, and note reclassification fires only on the exact value 'no'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the degraded-mode behavior when web search is unavailable/empty for Proposer A or the divergence round (e.g. emit no-consensus with an explicit 'OSS evidence unavailable' note rather than treating absence as a low-weight bucket).
evidence: Proposer A input: 'web search plus the code'; the research round is 'put symmetrically to both records'
No stated behavior when the web search fails, is rate-limited, or returns nothing — buckets cover record contents, not tool unavailability
T5b: an external call with no fallback/degraded-mode
findings.finding: Proposer A ('how do popular OSS projects handle this?') and the divergence research round both hard-depend on web search, but the plan states no degraded path when web search is unavailable or returns nothing usable. The four divergence buckets classify the record's contents, not a search outage, so a failed/empty web round has no defined outcome.
findings.location: Edit 2 — asymmetric proposers ('web search plus the code') and the divergence research round
scenarios: Web search is unavailable during a run: Proposer A cannot answer its question and the OSS side of the divergence round is empty — does the survivor default to no-consensus, or is convergence measured on incomplete inputs?
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence: if the web search is unavailable or returns no usable result, the affected side is marked 'evidence unavailable' (not 'never considered') and the survivor emits a no-consensus item flagged as such, so the outage is visible at Phase 4.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the prior_decision value AND its attached record (ticket/ADR/commit) are persisted on the Phase-2 survivor entry and travel on the Phase-2->Phase-3 gate carrier, so Phase 3 Proposer B and Phase 4 approval can read them.
evidence: verification.md line 204: 'the survivor set (each carrying validity, impact, citations, why_it_matters)' — the documented Phase-2->Phase-3 gate lists exactly these fields.

Plan Edit 1 adds only the HARDENING label to the persisted survivor record ('recorded on the survivor in the persisted Phase-2 audit record ... alongside validity/impact/citations/why_it_matters') and says prior_decision 'passes it through to Phase 4', but never states the prior_decision record (ticket/ADR/commit) is added to the survivor carrier.
Edit 2: 'Proposer B "how does this project already handle this?" (the record — tickets, ADRs, git log/blame, the Phase-2 prior_decision ...)'.
Edit 3: 'Surface the prior_decision record (ticket/ADR/commit, what was decided ...) at review time'.
findings.finding: The prior_decision record is consumed by Phase 3 (Proposer B reads 'the Phase-2 prior_decision') and by Phase 4 (approval.md must 'surface the prior_decision record'), but the plan never adds it to the Phase-2 -> Phase-3 gate carrier that transports survivor state.
findings.location: Edit 1 (verification.md audit record / gate) vs Edit 2 (remediation.md) and Edit 3 (approval.md)
scenarios: Phase 3 Proposer B tries to read the Phase-2 prior_decision but no field exists on the survivor set, so it re-derives it (defeating the 'the verifier surfaces the record' design) or omits it.
Phase 4 approval.md is told to surface the prior_decision record but the item/finding carries no such field.
findings.suggested_fix: In Edit 1, add prior_decision (+ its attached ticket/ADR/commit reference) to the persisted `## Survivors` entry and to the 'Gate to Phase 3' carrier list alongside validity/impact/citations/why_it_matters.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the adoption polarity in the bucket-to-outcome mapping: state which bucket ('Adopted and kept' vs 'Explicitly rejected') causes adoption of which side's move, so a high 'Explicitly rejected' answer does not adopt a reverted approach.
evidence: Bucket table: 'Explicitly rejected — adopted, then reverted, with stated reasons | high' and 'Adopted and kept — live counter-examples, named | high'.
Mapping: 'a high-weight answer on exactly one side adopts that side's move, tagged research-resolved'.

The research questions are polarity-bearing ('has the community explicitly rejected this project's approach, and has this project explicitly rejected the community's?'), so a high bucket can signal either endorsement or rejection of the side it lands on.
findings.finding: The bucket-to-outcome rule 'a high-weight answer on exactly one side adopts that side's move' does not disambiguate the two opposite-polarity high buckets: 'Explicitly rejected' (evidence AGAINST that side's move) and 'Adopted and kept' (evidence FOR it) both weigh high, so 'adopt that side's move' can mean adopting an approach the record shows was reverted.
findings.location: Edit 2 (remediation.md) — divergence research round, bucket table and bucket-to-outcome mapping
scenarios: Side A's answer lands in 'Explicitly rejected' (high) and Side B's is 'Never considered' (low): the rule fires 'high on exactly one side -> adopt that side's move', but that side's move is the one the record shows was reverted.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the mapping so that adoption follows the endorsing bucket: 'Adopted and kept' on one side adopts THAT side's move; 'Explicitly rejected' on one side adopts the OTHER side's move; any conflict or non-high/non-endorsing outcome -> no-consensus.
